newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Unions rejoin S.Africa power restructuring talks.
newsitem.headline: Unions rejoin S.Africa power restructuring talks.

text.p: The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and the National Union of Metalworkers of SA (Numsa) have agreed to rejoin talks on the restructuring and possible part privatisation of power utility Eskom.
A Public Enterprises Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday that the unions had agreed to come back on board following a meeting on Tuesday with Eskom Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau.
"The outcome of the meeting is that the unions have agreed to rejoin the Restructuring and Transformation Committee," Wandile Zote, spokesman for Sigcau, said.
"The meeting agreed to revitalise the Restructuring and Transformation Committee at Eskom in terms of the National Framework Agreement," he added.
Parties at the talks had also agreed to address areas of disagreement raised by the unions at a meeting at the beginning of the month.

Labour walked out of Eskom's Restructuring and Transformation Committee earlier this month, raising concerns about the possible sale of mothballed power stations or recommissioning of decommissioned plants, and a planned outsourcing deal between Eskom and IBM.
It was also worried about an internal regrouping of management within Eskom and the restructuring of the electricity distribution sector.

Eskom chief executive Allen Morgan said earlier this week government proposals to sell decommissioned stations could inject new competition into the South African market and bring foreign expertise on board.
Morgan told Reuters no decisions had yet been taken but benefits could flow to consumers.
Eskom was currently in the process of developing options around the proposals, looking at different alternatives for the decommissioned stations, he said.
